title: Doubled word scan and continuation
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $K$ a proposition, and $σ=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ a program register state. Suppose every register of $σ$ is at most $B$ and $p+2|\mathrm{bits}(tmp)|+2\le B$. Assume that whenever the word of binary digits of $tmp$ is doubled at position $p$ in $x$, the program started at the target stage with pointer $p+2|\mathrm{bits}(tmp)|+2$ and scratch register zero terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and has an accepting computation exactly when $K$ holds. Then the program started at the scan stage in state $σ$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and has an accepting computation exactly when both that doubled-word condition and $K$ hold.
hypotheses_covered: all nine registers of $\u001bσ$ are at most $B$
whenever the binary word of $tmp$ is doubled at position $p$ in $x$, the stated target-stage configuration has the specified termination, register bound, and acceptance semantics
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $K$ a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a
configuration of nine natural-number registers, each at most $B$. Suppose the input
pointer $p$ in $\sigma$ satisfies $p+2|\mathrm{bits}(\mathrm{tmp})|+2\le B$. If,
whenever the bits of $\mathrm{tmp}$ occur in $x$ starting at position $p$ with each bit
repeated twice and followed by $01$, the fixed program started after that block—with its
pointer advanced by $2|\mathrm{bits}(\mathrm{tmp})|+2$ and its scratch register set to
zero—terminates within the register bound and accepts exactly when $K$ holds, then
starting the program at the scan stage in configuration $\sigma$ terminates within the
register bound and accepts exactly when both that doubled-block condition and $K$ hold.
